subject: killer whale
title: Wild Orcas Keep Offering People Their Kill, Then Wait

scenes.text: Orcas are top predators. Some keep handing their food to humans.
Scientists collected 34 cases over twenty years, from Alaska to New Zealand and Norway.
The gifts included rays, a sea turtle, a seabird, even a strand of seaweed.
The orca swims up, drops the food near a person, and backs off.
In all but one case, it waited to see what the human would do. Some tried again.
Orcas share food with each other all the time. Now they're testing us.

description:
A 2025 study in the Journal of Comparative Psychology collected 34 cases from 2004 to 2024 in which wild killer whales approached people and offered prey, from California and Alaska to New Zealand, Argentina and Norway.
In all but one case the orca waited for a reaction; in seven it tried more than once. Researchers think it may be the same food sharing orcas use with each other.
Would you take the gift?
first_comment: Researchers say: don't accept. Watching is fine, but feeding wild orcas changes their behaviour. What would you have done?
